claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch was bishop of Antioch and died before 337.
Eustathius was born at Side in Pamphylia.
Eustathius was bishop of Beroea about 320 and became patriarch of Antioch shortly before the Council of Nicaea in 325.
At the Council of Nicaea, Eustathius distinguished himself zealously against the Arians.
Eustathius was deposed by a synod at Antioch in 327/330 and banished to Thrace by Emperor Constantine.
The work Oratio in inscriptione psalmorum graduum is listed with CPG number 3355.
The work survives only in fragments.
Eustathius was a thorough opponent of the school of Origen.
The only complete work by Eustathius is De Engastrimytho contra Origenem.
Eustathius's works were edited by J.H. Declerck in the Corpus Christianorum series.
